clue.text: Weight of foolish beauty cut

indicators.note: something cut has been trimmed, so the word for beauty loses its final letter

parts.note: dumb means stupid in informal use
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A cruel remark about the scales reading of a silly beauty queen who has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: DUMB plus BELLE without its last E gives DUMBBELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbbell is a short bar with weights at each end, lifted for exercise, so it is a type of weight.

clue.text: Strip joint supported by holy person

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported by something means sitting on top of it, so the holy person comes underneath

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A seedy strip club is propped up by a saint, which is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip joint' looks like one phrase, but strip is the definition and joint starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to strip someone of clothes, possessions or rights, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: The whisper is, odds going up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd, and odds gives it twice

explanation.surface: Gossip at the racecourse: the word is that the betting odds are lengthening.
explanation.walkthrough: Odds suggests betting, but it is the plural of odd, and rum is an old British word for odd. Two RUMs read upwards give MURMUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A murmur is a soft, low utterance, the same as a whisper or a rumour passed quietly.

clue.text: Show Guys and Dolls without the guys?

parts.words: Guys and Dolls without the guys?
parts.note: surface reading: a production of the musical with no men in it

parts.words: Guys and Dolls without the guys?
parts.note: setter's reading: dolls is slang for women, so an all-female company is a cast made up of broads

explanation.surface: Putting on the musical Guys and Dolls with only the women in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Broad is American slang for a woman, the same sense as doll in the musical's title; a cast of broads, run together, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast is to show a programme on television or radio, so the verb matches show.

clue.text: From despotic type, refuse to swallow it — he'll change

indicators.note: to swallow is to take something inside, so the rubbish word holds the rest

parts.note: litter is rubbish dropped in the street

indicators.note: change tells us the letters before it take a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A bossy tyrant refuses to accept something, insisting he will change instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun for rubbish, and the dash hides that 'it' and 'he'll' are the letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A little Hitler is an informal term for a petty official or person who acts like a tyrant.

clue.text: No progressive state succeeded with secret police

parts.note: the Stasi were East Germany's secret police
S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A political lament: a regressive country that won power with the help of secret police.
explanation.walkthrough: The secret police come first in the answer even though they are named last.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a condition of no change or development, a state that is not moving forward at all.

clue.text: Pole cat circles tree regularly

indicators.note: something that circles another goes all round it, enclosing it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word before it

parts.note: first and third letters

explanation.surface: A Polish cat runs rings around a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a nationality, but it means a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a carved emblem, and a totem pole is the post carrying those carvings, so pole stands for the answer.

clue.text: Nereid seeks Irishman with variable speed

parts.note: Sean is a common Irish first name
y is a standard algebraic variable
mph, miles per hour, is a unit of speed

explanation.surface: A sea goddess goes looking for an Irish man who drives at erratic speeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variable speed' reads as one phrase, but it splits into Y, an algebra letter, and MPH. 'Seeks' joins definition and wordplay loosely, as the book prints it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Nereids were the fifty daughters of Nereus, sea goddesses, so each one is a sea nymph.

clue.text: Source of heat does what it does: various things

parts.note: the sun is the source of the Earth's heat
the sun's familiar effect on wet things is to dry them

explanation.surface: A puzzled description of a heater that simply carries out its many functions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does what it does' is a riddle: what the sun does is dry things, so SUN DRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small items too minor to list separately, so assorted things.

clue.text: Drink, extremely short, going in here

indicators.note: a word that is short of something has lost its tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: very means to an extreme degree
the mouth is where food and drink go in

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink very quickly, and it goes straight in.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make 'extremely short' look like a description of the drink; it is two instructions, a word for extremely then a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermouth is a fortified wine flavoured with herbs, drunk as an aperitif or used in cocktails.

clue.text: Air pressure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tune or melody
second meaning: stress or tension put on something

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a single phrase about weather or tyres, but each is a separate meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a passage of melody and a heavy demand or force on someone, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Commissioned musician to beat time, staying in one key

parts.note: to trump is to beat, as with a trump card

indicators.note: a guest staying in a place is inside it, so the time letter goes within the key

parts.note: E major is a musical key
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A musician hired to keep the beat and stick to one key throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commissioned' plays on military rank: the trumpet major was the senior trumpeter of a cavalry regiment, a title Hardy used for a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet major was the regiment's chief trumpeter, an army musician holding a rank.

clue.text: Animal which adds up to a guinea?

wordplay.note: a guinea was 21 shillings: one shilling (S) plus one pound (QUID) adds up to it

explanation.surface: A question about a creature that could do the sums to reach a guinea.
explanation.walkthrough: In old British money a guinea was 21 shillings, that is a pound and a shilling; S is the shilling abbreviation and QUID is slang for a pound, so S + QUID gives SQUID.
explanation.definitionFit: A squid is a sea creature with ten arms, a mollusc and so an animal.

clue.text: Dignitary has to praise horse in speech

indicators.note: in speech means we only hear the words, so the spelling can change while the sound stays

parts.note: to laud is to praise
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A civic VIP is expected to say nice things about a horse in an address.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent LAUD MARE sounds like LORD MAYOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lord Mayor is the ceremonial head of a major city council, so a civic dignitary.

clue.text: Apologise when a "Hitch" line appears in Love Story, not western

indicators.note: something that appears in another sits inside it, so these letters go into the film word
not western tells us to drop W, the abbreviation for west

parts.note: a weepie is a tear-jerking film, and Love Story is a classic one
taken as written
to thumb a lift is to hitch one
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A film buff complains when a Hitchcock-style line turns up in the sentimental movie Love Story.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Story's famous line is 'Love means never having to say you're sorry', which nudges the solver toward apology; 'Hitch' in quotes is a verb for getting a lift, not Hitchcock.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat humble pie is an idiom for admitting you were wrong and apologising humbly.

clue.text: Approaching the side's eventual recovery

parts.note: late here means coming at the end of something
a rally is a recovery, as in prices or a team's fortunes

explanation.surface: A sports report: the team's comeback finally arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', linking the definition to a late rally; LATE RALLY run together is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Laterally means sideways, from or toward the side, which is how one approaches the side.

clue.text: One's insistent son should be given feather?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a feather is used to tickle, so it is a tickler; the question mark flags that

explanation.surface: A parent insisting their boy ought to be handed a feather.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition includes 'One's': someone who is insistent, read as one who insists.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler is a person who insists on strict observance of rules or standards.

clue.text: Getting is fetching

definitions.meaning: first meaning: turning into, as in getting cold
second meaning: attractive, suiting someone well

explanation.surface: A tiny maxim equating acquiring something with going to fetch it.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting and fetching both look like verbs of retrieving; one is changing state and the other is the adjective for attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming means growing or turning into something, and as an adjective it means flattering or attractive.

clue.text: As you can see, perfect scores

definitions.meaning: first meaning: normal sharp eyesight, as measured on an eye test
second meaning: a score is twenty, so two scores make the pair of numbers

explanation.surface: A judge remarks that the marks shown on the board are flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests scores as marks in a contest; here a score is simply the number twenty, twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-twenty vision is the standard for perfect sight, and two lots of twenty are two scores.

clue.text: Observation from blackface admitting extreme characters right for the foreign market

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the first piece holds the extremes within it

parts.note: a Blackface is a breed of sheep, and its only remark is baa
Z and A are the letters at the two ends of the alphabet
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A complaint that a remark made in blackface has been passed fit for export.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackface is not make-up here: the Scottish Blackface is a hill sheep common in Britain. BA(ZA)A then R.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is a market in the Middle East or South Asia, the classic market of foreign lands.

clue.text: Odysseus's home with a camcorder's captured

indicators.note: captured means held inside, so the answer is held within the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across with, a and camcorder

explanation.surface: A holiday film: Odysseus's homeland filmed on a video camera.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts inside 'with' and ends inside 'camcorder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ithaca is the Greek island ruled by Odysseus, to which he returns at the end of the Odyssey.

clue.text: Support reform of boss among elite

indicators.note: among places one thing in the middle of another

parts.note: the cream is the best of a group

indicators.note: a reform reshapes something, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Backing a shake-up of management among the top people in an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' reads as a verb in the surface, but it is the noun for a structural beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbeam is a horizontal beam that holds up or braces a structure, a type of support.

clue.text: Stop containing a power

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the first word wraps the a

parts.note: to stem a flow is to stop it
taken as written

explanation.surface: An order to halt something that holds a source of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside STEM after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is power in the sense of energy that drives engines, as in full steam ahead.

clue.text: Have a go at Sunday dinner

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to criticise someone severely
second meaning: the traditional British Sunday meal of cooked meat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a go at' looks like trying a dish, but it means attack someone in words. In Britain the Sunday roast is the classic family meal of roasted meat and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise them harshly, and a roast is the joint of meat cooked for Sunday lunch.

clue.text: Hang about, Eliot's trashed centre of Liverpool

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked, so the poet's name is broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the poet's name taken as written

indicators.note: centre of asks for the single middle letter of the following word

parts.note: the fifth of nine letters

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry: wait a minute, T.S. Eliot has been wrecking the middle of Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang about' sounds like an interjection meaning wait, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly without purpose, which is what hanging about means.

clue.text: Formal wear oriental at a party switched for cloak

parts.note: DJ is short for dinner jacket
E for eastern

indicators.note: switched means turned the other way, so the phrase a party runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: An eastern guest at a dinner swaps his formal suit for a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ and E stay in order; A BALL is read backwards to finish DJ-E-LLABA.
explanation.definitionFit: A djellaba is a loose hooded robe worn in North Africa, a kind of cloak.

clue.text: Authoritarian government curtailing diet

indicators.note: curtailing means cutting off the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a regimen is a prescribed course of diet or exercise

explanation.surface: A dictatorship cuts back on what its people can eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads curtailing as the regime limiting food; it is the instruction to drop the final N.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a government, especially one that rules in an authoritarian way.

clue.text: defined concrete jungle?

parts.note: the last word of the lost first half of the clue, kept only as padding here
surface reading: a bleak built-up city district
setter's reading: concrete is grey, so a concrete jungle is literally a region of that colour

explanation.walkthrough: The book's copy of this clue has lost its opening words, which probably read something like 'Something not clearly defined'; only the punning second half survives here.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a situation or topic that is unclear and falls between definite categories.
